operator_request: Start implementing WP-009; use no more than three subagents in parallel for implementation help and independent adversarial review through different lenses; harden concerns, risks, and gaps; clean Cargo/test artifacts when finished; close finished subagents; tolerate long waits on the loaded host; do not stop processes the assistant did not start; and preserve Ferric as a Rust-native yt-dlp replacement with no yt-dlp dependency.

authority_checked: current fforager-contracts, fforager-core, fforager-testkit, fforager-xtask, fixtures, and MODEL_MANUAL.md

sources_checked.evidence: Multi-resource fairness must reason about a user's dominant share rather than independent scalar permits; adaptive DRF remains later work because WP-009 freezes a simpler deterministic first policy.

Owned RAII permits release on Drop; FIFO acquire-many fairness can intentionally reserve a large queue head; cancelled acquisition loses its place. Ferric reuses these semantics without adding Tokio to fforager-core.
A bounded queue propagates consumer capacity upstream, while an unbounded queue admits indefinitely; Ferric additionally requires byte bounds because item bounds alone are insufficient.

Permutation testing is valuable but bounded and explicitly incomplete for parts of the C11 memory model; WP-009 must report model bounds and residual uncertainty rather than claim universal concurrency proof.
Bounded black-box crash testing enumerates finite operation/persistence prefixes and compares recovered state against an oracle; WP-009 adopts bounded prefix enumeration and explicit fault receipts.
Typestate can enforce persistence ordering, but WP-009 retains the already-versioned Ferric state-machine boundary and uses executable transition guards instead of introducing a parallel type system.
RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, and RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS provide an explicit rooted resolution contract; O_NOFOLLOW alone protects only the final component.
File fsync does not necessarily persist the containing directory entry, so rename durability requires separately acknowledged directory synchronization.
Same-filesystem replacement visibility and cross-filesystem EXDEV are distinct from durable persistence; the model keeps rename and sync acknowledgements separate.
File::sync_all reports close-time errors that Drop cannot; explicit acknowledgement is required before durable state advances.
std::fs::rename rejects separate filesystems and maps to different OS primitives; cross-volume copy/sync/rename must remain a separately modeled non-atomic boundary.
Security-sensitive path handling must inspect reparse points using handles and FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT rather than trusting normalized names.
Buffered file data requires explicit FlushFileBuffers acknowledgement; platform and filesystem support remain capability facts, not universal assumptions.
Handle-relative rename supports an explicit root directory; Ferric must separately verify final handle identity and volume before acknowledging confinement or replacement.
Operational job systems expose explicit bounded timeouts and observable job identity; this supports Ferric's timeout and trace requirements but does not define Ferric's scheduler.
Community reports reinforce that bounded-channel cycles can deadlock and cancellation/lifecycle ownership is easy to omit; used only to seed negative tests, never as contract authority.

Hugging Face supplied relevant timeout/resource examples; Civitai supplied download identity/size metadata but no durable-prefix implementation; X searches returned no inspectable primary implementation evidence. No mechanism was selected from these scans.

patterns_found: Atomic multi-resource admission must be one transaction; independent semaphores cannot prove no hold-and-wait.
Owned permits need Drop-based release plus explicit release receipts when outcome attribution matters.
Item-bounded queues still need byte bounds and simultaneous input/output reservation for transforming stages.
Fairness claims are conditional on explicit release/cancellation assumptions and need a deterministic queue/tie-break policy.
Crash proof is a bounded prefix exploration problem with independent recovery oracles and mutation-sensitive failures.
Rename visibility, data synchronization, directory synchronization, archive insertion, cleanup, and final reconciliation are separate acknowledgements.
Path confinement is handle-relative and capability-specific; normalization is not a security boundary.
Cross-volume and network filesystems require explicit degraded or rejected profiles rather than inherited local-filesystem claims.
reuse_opportunities: Extend the existing 13-dimensional ResourceVector, ResourceLedger, ByteCreditLedger, DurabilityPosition, StateMachine, JournalRecord, CommitState, ReconcileState, and FilesystemCapability types.
Reuse fforager-testkit fixture loading, deterministic lifecycle replay, public-boundary counterexamples, and stable invariant IDs.
Reuse fforager-xtask's proof-class reporting, change-evidence checks, architecture fixtures, and active-packet aggregation.
Reuse the existing MODEL_MANUAL resource/durability section and update only actually implemented commands and proof ceilings.
selected_approach: Keep fforager-core dependency-free beyond fforager-contracts; do not add Tokio, Loom, proptest, a database, Python, yt-dlp, or another runtime.
Promote existing pure models into versioned strict contracts plus deterministic bounded schedule/fault exploration.
Freeze strict FIFO head reservation with a deterministic per-owner active ceiling as the v1 fairness policy; adaptive DRF or weighted policies remain later evidence-driven work.
Add owned RAII resource/credit leases at the Ferric boundary so success, error, panic unwind, and cancellation drop paths release exactly once.
Generate machine-readable traces and reports that name concrete inputs, executed boundaries, expected and observed outcomes, proof class, and residual uncertainty.
Treat Windows NTFS as the supported local positive profile and Ubuntu WSL2 over v9fs as an explicit Unix rejected/degraded profile; do not claim native Linux filesystem durability from WSL interop.
rejected_options: Independent per-resource semaphores: rejected because they permit hold-and-wait and cannot atomically admit composite vectors.

Adding Tokio/Loom/proptest now: rejected because existing Ferric pure models and deterministic explorer can close the bounded prerequisite without another dependency; Loom's own documented incompleteness would not provide universal proof.
Replacing existing contracts with a new typestate hierarchy: rejected because it would duplicate accepted WP-005/WP-014 public boundaries and increase migration risk.
Treating std::fs::rename as durable commit: rejected because visibility, file sync, directory sync, archive, and reconciliation acknowledgements are distinct.
Claiming native Linux support from the WSL2 v9fs mount: rejected because the observed filesystem and host boundary differ from native ext4/xfs semantics.
Any yt-dlp/Python runtime, test, fixture generator, fallback, sidecar, or delegated path: rejected by project authority and the Operator's explicit constraint.

resource_vector_contract.ownership_rule: one non-cloneable owned lease releases exactly once on Drop or explicit finish
fairness_assumptions: Every active grant eventually releases, explicitly cancels, or unwinds.
Requests do not exceed configured capacity.
The queue head is never bypassed; once it fits, it is the next issued request.
resource_vector_contract.starvation_bound: Conditional on the assumptions, a queued request advances after at most the finite set of active grants ahead of it release and every earlier waiter is issued and released; no later waiter adds delay.

byte_credit_contract.reservation_rule: reserve every simultaneously live input and output byte before allocation
byte_credit_contract.ownership_rule: an unconsumed claim may transfer exactly once at a time; consumed attribution cannot be rewritten
byte_credit_contract.loss_policy: required bytes are lossless; lossy diagnostics require a separate declared budget and cannot consume recorder credit

exploration_profile.determinism: stable case IDs plus explicit seeds and lexicographic transition order
bounds: maximum active grants and queued requests
maximum byte claims and queue bytes
finite fault inventory across every durable prefix
bounded trace length with fail-closed overflow
required_failure_oracles: no queue item or byte bound violation
no durability position ahead of its prerequisite
no durable or terminal state before the full acknowledgement set

non_goals: Building the full scheduler, downloader, storage backend, FFmpeg adapter, or Phase 1 entrypoint.

minimum_controls: Every mutation is transactional or leaves state byte-for-byte unchanged.
Owned leases are non-cloneable and release through one identity-checked path.
Every variable-size queue exposes item and byte occupancy.
Every durable/terminal transition requires the complete effect acknowledgement set.
Fault cases retain concrete input, prefix, expected and observed recovery, and proof class.
Platform reports fail closed on unrecognized or mismatched profile identity.
Independent reviewers attack separate resource, durability/filesystem, and proof-integrity lenses.
plausible_failures: An integer boundary corrupts accounting after a failed release or queued dispatch.
A panic drops user work but leaves a ledger grant live.
Small jobs bypass a large head request indefinitely.
A transform owns input plus output while only one side is credited.
A checkpoint record becomes durable before the referenced bytes or directory entry.
A recovery model accepts archive-without-output or output-without-archive as success.
A WSL/v9fs result is mislabeled as native Linux filesystem proof.
A declaration-only fixture passes without changing executable behavior.
